items.title: What Makes Resolve Retreat, and Two Marvels Unique to the Bodhisattva Alone

items.zh: 有四因緣、能令菩薩退菩提心。何等為四？一、種姓不具；二、惡友所攝；三、於諸眾生悲心微薄，四、於極長時種種猛利無間無缺生死大苦難行苦行，其心極生怯畏驚怖。
items.en: Four conditions can cause a bodhisattva's resolve for awakening to retreat: lacking the lineage; being taken in by bad companions; having only thin compassion for beings; and, faced with the fierce, unbroken, unremitting suffering and difficult practice demanded over an extremely long time, the mind gives rise to genuine timidity, fear, and alarm.

items.zh: 如是四種心退因緣，與上發心四因相違，廣辯其相，如前應知。
最初發心堅固菩薩，略有二種不共世間甚希奇法。何等為二？一者、攝諸眾生皆為眷屬，二者、攝眷屬過所不能染。
items.en: A bodhisattva whose initial resolve is firm has, in brief, two marvellous qualities shared with no other being at all. What are the two? First, embracing every being as kin; second, being untouched by the faults that ordinarily accompany embracing kin.

items.zh: 攝眷屬過有其二種。謂於眷屬饒益損減、染污違順。如是二事，菩薩皆無。

items.title: Firm Resolve in Practice — Two Aspirations, Two Kinds of Effort, and a Superiority in Both Cause and Fruit

items.zh: 最初發心堅固菩薩，於諸眾生發起二種善勝意樂。一者、利益意樂，二者、安樂意樂。利益意樂者，謂欲從彼諸不善處，拔濟眾生，安置善處。安樂意樂者，謂於貧匱無依無怙諸眾生所，離染污心，欲與種種饒益樂具。
items.en: A bodhisattva of firm initial resolve gives rise to two excellent, superior aspirations towards beings: the aspiration to benefit, and the aspiration to bring happiness. The aspiration to benefit is the wish to rescue beings from unwholesome states and settle them in wholesome ones. The aspiration to bring happiness is the wish, free of any defiling motive, to give beneficial things to beings who are destitute, without support, and without protection.

items.zh: 最初發心堅固菩薩，有二加行。一、意樂加行，二、正行加行。意樂加行者，謂即利益安樂意樂日夜增長。正行加行者，謂於日夜能自成熟佛法加行，及於眾生隨能隨力，依前所說意樂加行，起與利益安樂加行。最初發心堅固菩薩，有二增長大善法門。一者、自利加行，能證無上正等菩提；二者、利他加行，能脫一切有情眾苦。如二增長大善法門，如是二種大善法聚、二種無量大善法藏，當知亦爾。最初發心堅固菩薩，由初發心求菩提故，所攝善法，比餘一切所攝善法，有二種勝。一者、因勝，二者、果勝。
謂諸菩薩所攝善法，皆是無上正等菩提能證因故，所證無上正等菩提是此果故，比餘一切聲聞、獨覺所攝善法尚為殊勝，何況比餘一切有情所攝善法。是故菩薩所攝善法，比餘一切所攝善法，因果俱勝。
items.en: The wholesome practices a bodhisattva takes up are all causes capable of realising unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and that same awakening is their fruit — surpassing even the wholesome practices of hearers and solitary buddhas, let alone those of every other being. For this reason, a bodhisattva's wholesome practices surpass every other being's in both cause and fruit alike.

items.title: Section: The Concrete Blessings of Firm Resolve — Universal Reverence, and Protection Beyond a King's

items.zh: 最初發心堅固菩薩，略有二種發心勝利。一者、初發菩提心已，即是眾生尊重福田，一切眾生皆應供養；亦作一切眾生父母。二者、初發菩提心已，即能攝受無惱害福。
items.en: A bodhisattva of firm initial resolve gains, in brief, two benefits from that resolve. First, the very moment the resolve for awakening is raised, one becomes a field of merit deserving all beings' reverence, worthy of everyone's offering, and, in effect, a parent to every being. Second, the very moment the resolve is raised, one gains harmless merit.

items.zh: 由此菩薩成就如是無惱害福，得倍輪王護所守護；由得如是護所護故，若寢、若寤、若迷悶等，一切魍魎、藥叉、宅神、人非人等不能嬈害。又此菩薩轉受餘生，由如是福所攝持故，少病、無病，不為長時重病所觸。於諸眾生所作義利，能以身語勇猛而作。常為眾生宣說正法，身無極倦，念無忘失，心無勞損。
items.en: By this harmless merit, the bodhisattva is protected by a guard exceeding even a universal monarch's; sleeping, waking, or even unconscious, no goblin, spirit, household deity, human, or nonhuman being is able to cause harm. In whatever future rebirth is taken, this same merit ensures little or no illness, never touched by prolonged serious sickness … whatever benefits beings, one acts on boldly with body and speech; constantly teaching beings the true Dharma, the body never grows exhausted, mindfulness never fails, and the mind never wears down.

items.zh: 菩薩本性住種姓時，一切麁重性自微薄；既發心已，所有麁重轉復輕微。謂身麁重及心麁重。

items.title: Section: The Resolve Chapter Closes — Even a Bodhisattva's Rare Fall to Hell Becomes Productive

items.zh: 若餘眾生為欲息滅疾疫災橫，所用無驗呪句、明句，菩薩用之尚令有驗，何況驗者。成就增上柔和忍辱，能忍他惱，不惱於他；見他相惱，深生悲惱。忿、嫉、諂等諸隨煩惱，皆能摧伏，令勢微薄；或暫現行，速能除遣。
items.en: Even a formula that fails when used by others to dispel plague or disaster becomes effective in a bodhisattva's hands — how much more so one already effective … endowed with supreme gentleness and patience, able to bear others' provocation without provoking others in turn, and, seeing another provoked, feeling deep compassion for them instead … anger, envy, flattery, and every such derivative affliction are subdued, their force made faint — and should any briefly flare up, it is swiftly dispelled.

items.zh: 隨所居止國土城邑，於中所有恐怖、鬪諍、饑饉過失，非人所作疾疫災橫，未起不起，設起尋滅。又此最初發心菩薩，或於一時生極惡趣那落迦中，多分於此那落迦趣速得解脫。受小苦受，生大厭離；於彼受苦諸眾生等，起大悲心。
items.en: Wherever such a bodhisattva dwells — whatever land or town — fear, conflict, famine, and disasters caused by nonhuman beings either never arise there, or, if they do, are quickly quelled … and should this same bodhisattva of firm initial resolve, at some point, be reborn even in the most severe hell realm, in most cases swift release follows; only slight suffering is felt, giving rise to profound revulsion towards its cause, and deep compassion for the other beings suffering there.

blocks.text: What weakens the resolve, and the extraordinary blessings of a firm one. A passage (0482a16) is untranslated.

Lacking the lineage; being taken in by bad companions (Master Cháng Bǎi: those around one don't want one to practise); thin compassion; and fear of the long, unbroken suffering and difficult practices.

One with a firm resolve "embraces every being as kin" (Venerable Miào Jìng: good people are my friends; bad people are my friends too), and "is untouched by the faults that usually accompany such embracing", such as attachment.
To **benefit** (rescue beings from the unwholesome and settle them in the good) and to bring **happiness**. Master Cháng Bǎi: kindness gives happiness; compassion removes suffering.

Two efforts: of aspiration (these wishes growing day and night) and of actual practice (ripening the Buddha's qualities in oneself, and helping beings as one can). Two great gates of growth: self-benefit (leading to awakening) and benefiting others (freeing beings from suffering). The good gathered by the resolve surpasses all other good, in its **cause** and in its **fruit**.

At the moment of the resolve, one becomes "a field of merit deserving all beings' reverence". One is protected "by a guard exceeding even a universal monarch's": no spirit can harm one, sleeping or waking. Even a charm that fails for others works for such a one. Where such a person lives, fear, famine, and conflict subside. And if ever reborn in hell, "one is swiftly released, and moved to compassion for those there".

quiz.q: The second cause of retreat: "taken in by bad companions." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: teachers and friends around one won't raise the resolve, and one is influenced to retreat
quiz.why: "Being taken in by bad companions." Master Cháng Bǎi: the teachers and friends around one don't want to raise the resolve for unsurpassed awakening, and one is influenced to retreat.

quiz.q: The first marvel: "embracing every being as kin." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: good people are my friends, and so are bad people
quiz.why: "First, embracing every being as kin." Venerable Miào Jìng: good people are my good friends, and bad people are my good friends too.

quiz.q: The aspirations to benefit and to bring happiness — how does Master Cháng Bǎi map them to kindness, compassion, and cause/fruit?
options: kindness gives happiness, compassion removes suffering (benefit); benefit is cause, happiness fruit
quiz.why: "The aspiration to benefit, and the aspiration to bring happiness." Master Cháng Bǎi: kindness gives happiness (bringing beings happiness), compassion removes suffering (benefiting beings); conceptually, benefit is cause and happiness fruit.

quiz.q: Benefit is "rescuing beings from unwholesome states, settling them in wholesome ones." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say about the Buddha?
options: Śākyamuni founded no hospitals or old-age homes
quiz.why: "The aspiration to benefit is the wish to rescue beings from unwholesome states and settle them in wholesome ones." Venerable Miào Jìng: Śākyamuni Buddha didn't run hospitals or old-age homes — he didn't do that. The point: benefit means leading beings from wrong to good.

quiz.q: "Protected by a guard double a universal monarch's." How do the masters read "double"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: a monarch has 500 blue-clad spirit guards, the bodhisattva 1,000; Miào Jìng: merit equal to two monarchs' — really one's past merit
quiz.why: "By this harmless merit, the bodhisattva is protected by a guard exceeding even a universal monarch's." Master Cháng Bǎi: a monarch has 500 blue-clad spirits guarding him; a bodhisattva who has raised the resolve has 1,000. Venerable Miào Jìng: his merit equals two monarchs' merit.

quiz.q: Once the resolve is raised, one is "a parent to every being." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: beings' noble path arises through the bodhisattva's teaching — so like a parent
quiz.why: "The very moment the resolve for awakening is raised, one becomes a field of merit deserving all beings' reverence … and, in effect, a parent to every being." Venerable Miào Jìng: all beings' noble path arises through the bodhisattva's teaching — so it's as if a parent.

quiz.q: A bodhisattva "reborn even in hell, swiftly released." What story does Master Cháng Bǎi tell?
options: in the hell of fiery carts, asking that his companion's rope be tied to his own neck so he alone pulls the cart
quiz.why: "Should this same bodhisattva of firm initial resolve, at some point, be reborn even in the most severe hell realm, in most cases swift release follows." Master Cháng Bǎi tells of the fiery-cart hell: "Tie my companion's rope to my neck — let me pull the cart alone."
